provenance.licenceSource: An 1855 publication: the work is in the public domain, which is a positive claim that no terms attach rather than an absence of information.
provenance.note: Georeferenced north-up from four control points whose coordinates were obtained from OpenStreetMap via Nominatim, © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL. Four coordinates are not a substantial extract, so no share-alike obligation is asserted; the attribution is recorded because the figures came from somewhere. The plate is INK, NOT MEASUREMENT: sampling its pixels returns the colour of a line.

params.label: Snow’s Map 2, as published
params.mapTitle: Snow’s Map 2, 1855: which water company supplied which part of south London
params.mapSubtitle: The plate as published, drawn at its georeferenced extent. The blue and the red washes are the two companies’ supply territories and the purple is the zone where both companies’ pipes are intermingled, which is the whole of Snow’s design.
params.mapSourceNote: John Snow, On the Mode of Communication of Cholera, 2nd edn (London: John Churchill, 1855), Map 2. Plate from Project Gutenberg ebook 72894, 1,002 × 788 pixels, georeferenced north-up at about 15.8 m per pixel. Context: a plate is ink, not measurement.
